## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Hosted workflows using `isolate-agent` can now share installed Playwright browsers, uv-managed Python versions, and mise tools with the isolated agent. The action gives the agent a private, writable runtime directory and passes through those tool-location settings only when the agent can access the directories; inaccessible locations are dropped and logged.

The setup and troubleshooting wiki now explains how to configure shared tool installs and documents related isolation behavior, including private XDG roots and provider-key proxy limits. [#2232](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2232) [#2231](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2231)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Published `fro-bot/agent` installs could be rejected by `isolate-agent` when invoked through a repository’s composite action, because the runner points `GITHUB_ACTION_PATH` at the wrapper rather than the installed action. Preflight now identifies the install from the running `dist/main.js` bundle and validates the corresponding `_actions` path against the runner-provided repository and ref.

Local `uses: ./` installs remain refused, and the action’s main and post stages continue to resolve to the same reference-derived installation. [#2225](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2225)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Isolated Action runs could fail command lookups and Git checks even when the tools and checkout were available: inaccessible runner-owned PATH directories caused `EACCES` instead of `ENOENT`, and Git rejected the runner-owned checkout when system and global config were disabled. The Action now filters PATH entries to directories the agent can enter and passes the checkout as `safe.directory` through environment-based Git configuration.

Real-runner coverage now checks both missing-command behavior and checkout trust when `HOME`, global Git config, and system Git config are overridden. These changes address 14 of the 15 false failures observed in the remediation job; the remaining failure was not explained by the probe and is not addressed here. [#2222](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2222)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Isolated agents now have their own XDG data, config, cache, and state directories under their home, preventing tools that follow XDG from writing into read-only runner directories. Each directory’s `opencode` entry links back to the runner-provided location, so the server’s database, logs, and configuration remain there while other tools keep their own data with the agent. This also lets XDG-aware tools such as pnpm use their standard locations without separate environment-variable overrides.

The change preserves the existing runner paths for session recovery and cache saving, and keeps bun’s cache explicitly configured because it does not follow XDG. The setup now requires `ln`, and the real-runner checks cover pnpm’s store and writes to XDG cache and data locations. [#2219](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2219)


<details><summary>Full changelog</summary>

</details>

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When `isolate-agent` is enabled, agents can now run Bun and pnpm installed in the runner’s home, without receiving write access to those installation roots. The action grants read/execute access only to qualifying runner-owned directories on the agent’s `PATH`, and rejects grants that would expose sensitive or writable locations.

Python package workflows are also isolated from the runner’s read-only XDG directories: uv and pip caches, managed Python installations, and tool installations now live under the agent’s own home. Project virtual environments remain in the checkout, and these environment changes do not apply when isolation is disabled. [#2217](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2217) [#2218](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2218)

Successful isolation checks are now visible in info-level logs: the preflight read-only view probe reports its pass and elapsed time, and sandbox teardown reports when the launch namespace is confirmed empty. Failure reporting is unchanged, and these success logs are emitted only when `isolate-agent` is enabled. [#2215](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2215)
